lead: everyone in this town has stood inside something you put up. asked what you are like, they stall — no first impression of you is in circulation anywhere. you had each of them complete inside one evening.
sun: a first meeting with you gives the other person nothing to take away. the arrangement gets made, it holds from the day it goes up, and a thing that works from the start supplies no occasion on which anybody considers who set it there. so the people who spend their whole week inside your work carry a clear picture of it and no impression of its maker. thirty years of contact, nothing accumulating.
moon: your reading of them was finished inside a quarter of an hour and it did not loosen. what came off a pause, and the order two names were said in, has held through fifteen years of evidence nobody needed. so it runs one way, permanently: you have a whole person from one evening, and that person has a door that opens and a room that has never given trouble.
pull: you had them by the end of the first evening and you have them still. what they got that evening was somewhere that works, and nothing has been added to it since.
tension: what gets said about you is procedural — reliable, straightforward, sorted it in a week — and on some people that file is fifteen years old and closed. meanwhile a stranger's third sentence decided which side of the wall he would live on, and he has lived on that side since, with the matter never coming up. the arrangement does the declining, nobody is refused out loud, and no occasion has come up on which it would be said.
cost: a stranger gets placed correctly and provided for inside a fortnight, at whatever distance suits, with nothing discussed and nobody assessed where they can hear it. the exchange never evens up. you are holding finished readings of two hundred people at the resolution they were taken at, and the two hundred are holding a room that has never asked them for anything and an evening with no event in it.

lead: somebody tidies a problem in the corridor before knocking, every time, and has done for twenty years. what reaches your desk is the cleaned version of a place that runs on arrangements you wrote in a bad year.
sun: the rota, the route the money takes, the order a difficult meeting goes in — all of it came out of your hands in a stretch nobody now remembers, and nothing in it has needed adjusting since. that is the difficulty. an arrangement that works produces no moment where anybody thinks about it, so the institution meets your twenty years as its own ordinary condition, and where any of it came from never arises.
moon: and the seat makes the room careful. people arrive at their best, take their mess elsewhere, and hand you an edited account out of respect rather than fear. the carriage does not switch off between meetings, so no register is available in which a junior could hear the question as real. what comes upward is filtered by rank, and rank cannot be set down for an afternoon.
pull: the structure holds so nothing is reported, and the seat is steady so nothing is confided, and twenty years of both has produced a place that runs beautifully and tells you nothing.
tension: at a retirement do somebody said you were born to it, warmly and in public, and it settled nothing, because praise from a room on its best behaviour weighs what its silence weighs. the private version is whether you are owed a position you are also quietly holding up, and it can be put to nobody: a question from that chair is received as an instruction, and the answer comes shaped to please.
cost: two decades pass in that institution without a jam, and the people inside have a senior who never makes them nervous — two separate pieces of work, both yours. neither produces a sight of anything straining. difficulties are met and settled a floor beneath you, inside structures you designed, by people who would not dream of raising them, so the strongest claim available is that nothing has come up.

lead: they can describe you for ten minutes without arriving at one thing you have made. the description is warm, it is accurate, and every item in it is a property of your size rather than a decision of yours.
sun: what you put up holds twenty people and asks nothing of them, which is the point of it and why it appears in nobody's account of you. attention needs an edge to land on, and the thing you make has no moment: it went up, it works, it will be working in thirty years. so the looking arrives, stops on the person, and the two of you are in one room with only one visible.
moon: you get looked at constantly. what registers about you was set at a size you had no say in, and no gathering has ever received a reduced version, because none exists to hand out. the spread goes in ahead of you and the room reads plenty. so the most present thing at every occasion held inside your work is you, and the work has never come up.
pull: the room registers you before you have spoken and has never once considered the wall behind it. you are both. only one of you has a surface.
tension: a mild reservation from you lands as a scene. anything you take a position on arrives at your own size, and no quiet version of the sentence exists: either a rule you wrote gets thrown out for a poor reason with nothing said, or the meeting becomes about your feelings. and the reputation is geniality, which spends on atmosphere and nothing else. the rule goes, argued down by somebody with a quarter of your standing.
cost: people loosen the minute you come in, and then live for years inside an arrangement of yours that has never asked anything of them, and they experience the first as you and the second as the building. affection arrives in quantity, on time, entirely genuine. when weight is what the situation needs, there is none to draw on, and three decades of the other has left nothing to point at.

lead: the place you set up eleven years ago still has five people inside it and your handwriting on the rota. you finished with the whole of it in one season, and what you owe it has never been late.
sun: attendance was never part of how it stands. the load goes where you sent it, the boundary holds, and the arrangement is indifferent to whether you are in the room or have been gone four years — that indifference was designed in, and it is why nothing came down when you went. the people inside registered a change in who was about and none in the conditions their week happens under, which is accurate.
moon: fourteen stations separate your two lights on a road of twenty-eight, so each of them stands on the outside of the other, and no year of yours has put them on the same side. one end raises things meant to outlast everybody inside them. the other finishes absolutely, in one season, taking the season with it. what a finish here leaves standing is the obligation, met to the day.
pull: nothing in that place has slipped since the autumn you stopped caring about it, and that is all the evidence they have that you never did.
tension: the person who set it up still looks after the place — that is the sentence, said warmly, to new arrivals, eleven years on. the accurate version needs both halves at their own size: it ended completely, and every obligation has been met since without a lapse. produced in that room, the first half eats the second, and what they hear is that eleven years of provision were performance.
cost: you can finish with a thing entirely without one person underneath it losing anything. most endings take the arrangement with them; yours leave it standing at full strength, staffed, with the money arriving. you can also pay into something you feel nothing for, exactly, for years, with no drift in the amount or the date. what that builds is an unbroken record of care with nobody inside it.
